Team

Two partners, one team

A dealmaker who has built and sold companies, and an ex-McKinsey advisor.

Partner

Kacper Kossowski-Gerlach

Over 25 years building, running and selling companies, with deep roots in coffee. Kacper co-founded a specialty roastery, scaled it into one of Poland’s leading players, and sold it to an international group. He later ran operations inside a large organisation and raised capital for new ventures. He advises on sell side and buy side transactions, capital raising and transaction readiness. Kacper knows the deal from every side: owner, seller, buyer and investor.

Partner

Michał Kraszewski

Over 20 years in strategy consulting, including at McKinsey & Company. Michał advises boards and investors on corporate and business strategy, M&A and post merger integration. He has worked across energy, utilities, environmental services, the public sector and consumer. His work covers strategy design and implementation, operating model and cost programmes, pricing and commercial strategy, and strategic alliances and shared services platforms. He turns complex, high stakes decisions into a plan a board can act on.

Selected transactions

Representative transactions

Sell side

Coffee roastery

Specialty roaster, sale to a strategic buyer
Revenue~EUR 8.0m
EBITDA (margin)~EUR 0.9m · ~11%
Enterprise value~EUR 6.0m
EV / EBITDA~6.5–7.0×
EV / Revenue~0.75×
Structure~80% cash / ~20% earn-out
Earn-out24 months · EBITDA retention
BuyerStrategic (international group)
Process~8 months · 2 binding offers

What drove value. A premium roaster brand and repeatable wholesale contracts lifted the multiple above the size-class median.

Sell side

Coffee distributor

Regional distributor, sale to a strategic consolidator
Revenue~EUR 12.5m
EBITDA (margin)~EUR 1.6m · ~13%
Enterprise value~EUR 12.0m
EV / EBITDA~7.0–7.5×
EV / Revenue~0.95×
Structure~75% cash / ~25% earn-out
Earn-out24 months · gross-margin retention
BuyerStrategic (sector consolidator)
Process~9 months · 3 binding offers

What drove value. Above-market margins signalled value-added distribution, not commodity resale, and pulled the multiple toward the top of the range.

For context: lower mid-market F&B typically trades at ~5–8× EBITDA, with 15–30% of consideration deferred as earn-out. Brands and value-added players sit at the upper end; commodity distribution at the lower. Price is set in the final weeks of a competitive process, by the number of credible bidders, not the opening ask.
